newsitem.title: CHINA: China offshore oil output seen at 16 mln T in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China offshore oil output seen at 16 mln T in 1997.

text.p: China's offshore crude output is expected to reach 16 million tonnes in 1997, up from 15.01 million tonnes last year, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) would launch 15 large-scale offshore oil and gas fields and petrochemical projects in 1997, a three-fold increase over last year, the official agency said.
Huge potential remained to be tapped in China's offshore reserves, with proven geological offshore oil reserves already totalling 1.3 billion tonnes, it quoted CNOOC President Wang Yan as saying.

China had recently discovered a group of large offshore oil and gas fields, including the 32-6 oil field in Bohai Bay with expected reserves of 200 million tonnes and the Nanbao 35-2 oil field in Bohai Sea with 100 million tonnes, it said.
A recently-discovered gas field in the Yinggehai Sea had expected reserves of 50 billion cubic metres, it said.
These fields would guarantee sustainable offshore oil development in coming years, it quoted Wang as saying but gave no details.
